tasks.short: Plan and supervise staff-led recreation activities

steps.what: Read booked recreational and entertainment activities in the {CALENDAR}.
Draft an unsaved run sheet of those activities.
Check the run sheet against the booked activities.
File only the accepted activity run sheet in the {DOCS}.
Direct staff who lead sports, aquatics, games or performing arts.
Supervise the activity and stop it if a guest is at risk.

tasks.design: She reads the day's recreational and entertainment bookings in the {CALENDAR}. Those bookings are the only input. A deterministic sheet groups activity, time and place and does not save and does not choose staff. She checks it against the bookings. A separate step files only that accepted sheet in the {DOCS}. She still directs staff and still supervises sports, aquatics, games and performing arts on the floor.
tasks.previous_blocker: The day's activities sat in the booking list, and the run sheet was copied by hand before the floor opened.
tasks.enabler_now: The booking already holds activity, time and place, so a sheet can group those fields for her to accept or reject.
tasks.still_hard: Seeing that an activity is unsafe, and stopping it, still happens on the floor.
tasks.human_edge: She is in the room and can see the guest and the staff member.
tasks.altitude: She still spends the session on the floor. She no longer copies the run sheet, but she still accepts it before it is filed.

reach.task: lead a booked session of games or a pool activity
reach.learn: which booking must be on the run sheet before the session starts

evidence.claim: She still directs staff and still supervises the activity on the floor. The only shorter work is writing and filing the run sheet from bookings she read. Model knowledge.
Annex III 4(b) applies if an AI tool allocates shifts based on individual behaviour or personal traits, or monitors staff performance.

assumptions: The {CALENDAR} booking already names activity, time and place. She reads those fields in s1. The sheet only groups them. If a field is missing she types it. The sheet does not invent it and does not choose who works.
Filing the accepted sheet in the {DOCS} is inside the centre, for staff. It is not a message to guests. A wording change voids the filing.
Directing staff and supervising the floor are not shortened. Talking to staff in the room is not a send outside the organisation.
The 10 already-counted hours are the check in s3 and are not subtracted again. The 4 incremental hours are rewrites when she rejects a sheet.
No shift is allocated from behaviour or personal traits, so the annex III 4(b) use is not this sheet.
unknowns: Whether today's bookings already store activity, time and place as separate fields.
How often she currently writes the plan down, rather than keeping it in her head.
research_questions: What share of run sheets she rejects because a booking changed after she read it.

already_counted.description: Checking the sheet against the bookings she read is already in s3.

incremental.description: Rewriting a rejected run sheet herself, beyond the check already in s3.

approvals.approved_version: Activity run sheet she accepted in s3: activity, time and place copied from the bookings she read, with no staff assignment added. A wording change voids it.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: On a day she keeps the plan in her head and rewrites the sheet, only filing a sheet she already accepted is shorter, about 4. On a day the bookings are stable she accepts the draft, so both the writing and the filing are shorter, about 11. The 4 hours of rewrite upkeep are already taken off the central 18.

tasks.short: Direct and coordinate recreation workers on duty

steps.what: Read which entertainment and recreation workers are on duty.
Direct entertainment and recreation workers onto the activities that need cover.
Coordinate cover when one related worker leaves an activity.

tasks.design: She reads the duty list already posted in the {DOCS}, then directs entertainment and recreation workers onto the activities that need them, and coordinates cover when someone leaves the floor. Nothing is drafted, published or sent.
tasks.previous_blocker: Nothing blocked speaking to a worker who is standing next to her.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new removes the direction or the cover decision.
tasks.still_hard: Seeing who can leave an activity without leaving guests unattended still happens on the floor.
tasks.human_edge: She can see the floor and the worker at the same time.
tasks.altitude: Her day on the floor does not change. She still directs workers and still decides cover.

reach.task: move to the post the supervisor names
reach.learn: which post is uncovered when a colleague leaves

evidence.claim: Directing and coordinating workers on the floor stays with her and is not shortened. Model knowledge.
Without a collective rule, a roster is announced at least 28 days ahead; where work makes that impossible, working times at least 4 days ahead.

assumptions: Nothing is built, so incremental hours are zero. No step is shortened.
The duty list she reads was already posted. This task does not publish a roster and does not change working times.
Talking to a worker on the floor is not a send outside the organisation.
The {DOCS} item here is the duty list already on file.
unknowns: Whether the duty list is a posted document or only a name on a wall.
research_questions: How often cover on the day changes someone's working time, which would be a roster change outside this task.

incremental.description: No new upkeep, because nothing is built.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A floor hour is unchanged: she still reads who is on duty, still directs entertainment and recreation workers, and still coordinates cover. No step is shorter, so the saving is zero.

steps.what: Write vacancy points for the staff role: hours, skills and place.
Draft an unsaved advert to recruit those staff.

loop.input: The vacancy points she wrote in s1: role, hours, skills and place.
loop.output: An unsaved advert in sentences. Nothing is posted.
loop.check: Every duty and hour in the advert is compared with a point she wrote. A pay rate, a qualification or a promise she did not write is rejected. An empty role or empty hours blocks acceptance.
loop.stop: One pass. If she rejects the draft she writes the advert herself and nothing is posted.
loop.why_not_simpler: A field copy cannot turn short points into an advert an applicant can read without adding or dropping a duty.

steps.what: Check every line and accept that exact advert.
Post only the accepted advert in the {ATS}.
Read each application for that staff vacancy.
Interview the applicants she chose to meet.
Decide which applicant to hire as one of the staff members.

tasks.design: She writes the vacancy points. A bounded draft turns those points into an unsaved advert and does not post it. She checks every line. A separate step posts only that accepted advert in the {ATS}, where applicants outside the centre can read it. She still reads every application, still interviews, and still decides which person to hire. No tool ranks or rejects applicants.
tasks.previous_blocker: The advert was rewritten by hand into the recruitment system, and a draft could add a duty she had not stated.
tasks.enabler_now: The recruitment system can post an advert she has already accepted, and a bounded draft can be checked line by line against her points.
tasks.still_hard: Judging an applicant in the interview still sits with her.
tasks.human_edge: She knows the floor the person would join, and she hears the answer.
tasks.altitude: She still chooses who to hire. She no longer retypes the advert, but she still accepts the wording before it is posted.

reach.learn: which line of an advert must match the points they wrote before it is posted

evidence.claim: The advert is drafted from points she wrote. She still reads applications, interviews, and decides who to hire. The post sends only the advert she accepted. Model knowledge.
A tool that ranks or rejects applicants is an employment use of the EU AI Act. This design does not rank or reject anyone. Model knowledge.

assumptions: She writes the points before the draft: role, hours, skills and place. The draft does not invent a pay rate or a qualification. Nothing is posted until s4.
Posting the accepted advert is a send outside the organisation. It is its own step. Interviewing an applicant in the room is not that send. The hire decision is not a message.
No application is scored. She reads each one herself.
The 10 already-counted hours are the check in s3 and are not subtracted again. The 5 incremental hours are rewrites when she rejects an advert.
Consent and access days cover applicant data in the {ATS} and a processor agreement.
unknowns: Whether she may post to the {ATS} herself or must hand the accepted advert to a recruiter.
Whether the offer itself is a later written send, which would be a separate gated step not built here.
research_questions: What share of adverts she rejects because the draft added a duty.

already_counted.description: Checking the advert against the points she wrote is already in s3.

incremental.description: Rewriting a rejected advert herself, beyond the check already in s3.

approvals.approved_version: Vacancy advert she accepted in s3: role, hours, skills and place, with no pay rate or qualification she did not write. A wording change voids it.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the role is new she rewrites the advert, so only posting wording she wrote herself is shorter, about 4. When the vacancy repeats she accepts the draft, so both the writing and the post are shorter, about 12. The 5 hours of rewrite upkeep are already taken off the central 20.

tasks.short: Inform workers of a group's special needs

steps.what: Read the booking for specific groups and their interests and special needs.
Draft an unsaved briefing of those interests and special needs.

loop.input: The booking text she read in s1: the group, the interests stated, and the special needs stated.
loop.output: An unsaved briefing that lists only those interests and needs. Nothing is filed.
loop.check: Every interest and every need in the briefing is compared with the booking text she read. A medical conclusion, a diet, or a need the booking did not state is rejected. An empty briefing blocks acceptance.
loop.stop: One pass. If she rejects the draft she briefs from the booking and nothing is filed.
loop.why_not_simpler: A field copy cannot turn a free-text booking into a briefing for workers without adding or dropping a need.

steps.what: Check each stated need and accept that exact briefing.
File only the accepted briefing in the {DOCS}.
Inform workers in person about those groups' interests and special needs.

tasks.design: She reads the booking for the group's interests and special needs. A bounded draft restates only what she read and does not file it. She checks each need. A separate step files only that accepted briefing in the {DOCS}. She still informs the workers in person. The spoken briefing is not a send outside the organisation.
tasks.previous_blocker: The needs were buried in a free-text booking, and the note she left for the next shift could add a need that was not stated.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded draft can list only needs she has already read, and she can reject a line before anything is filed.
tasks.still_hard: Saying the need so the worker actually changes what they do still happens in person.
tasks.human_edge: She knows which need, if missed, would put a guest at risk.
tasks.altitude: She still tells workers the needs herself. She no longer rewrites the note, but she still accepts it before it is filed.

reach.task: hear a group's stated needs before a class

evidence.claim: She still informs workers in person. The draft only restates interests and special needs she read on the booking. Model knowledge.
A working and rest-time arrangement, and a time clock that can watch attendance or performance, need works council consent.
A group's stated needs can include health information. The briefing is filed only after she accepts the wording. Model knowledge.

Filing the accepted briefing is inside the centre. Informing workers in person is a talk with colleagues, not a send outside the organisation.
The briefing is about the visiting group, not a clock on staff. If the store is later used to score staff, stop. That would need works council consent.
The 12 already-counted hours are the check in s3 and are not subtracted again. The 4 incremental hours are rewrites when she rejects a briefing.
Consent and access days cover storing special-needs text and who on the staff may open that note.
unknowns: Whether the booking states needs in a field or only in free text.
Whether a parent or a school has agreed that staff may read those needs.
research_questions: What share of briefings she rejects because the booking was too vague to restate.

already_counted.description: Checking each need against the booking she read is already in s3.

approvals.approved_version: Briefing she accepted in s3: the group's interests and special needs as stated on the booking, with no medical conclusion added. A wording change voids it.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the booking is vague she writes the briefing herself, so only filing a note she already wrote is shorter, about 3.
